process_notes.ME: The Maine PUC issues certificates of public convenience and necessity for lines of 69 kV+ (35-A M.R.S. 3132; cases in the PUC CMS at mpuc-cms.maine.gov); in Aug 2026 it selected CMP/Avangrid's 1,200 MW Pittsfield - Haynesville line (Docket 2026-00033), but CMP targets 2033 service, and ISO-NE's TIDE LTTP projects are listed for 2032-12, both outside the window.
process_notes.NH: The Site Evaluation Committee (RSA 162-H) certifies lines over 200 kV, or over 100 kV and 10 miles outside existing ROW; since Dec 2025 its dockets sit in the PUC Virtual File Room (SEC- prefix). The only active line case is SEC 25-072 (X-178, 115 kV).
process_notes.VT: The PUC issues certificates of public good under 30 V.S.A. 248 (and 248a for telecom); VELCO posts its filings. 2023-2026 filings are 115 kV or substation-device projects (e.g., 25-1259-PET Sandbar power-flow controller).
process_notes.MA: The Energy Facilities Siting Board approves lines of 69 kV+ over 1 mile under G.L. c.164 s.69J, with parallel DPU Section 72/zoning petitions. Its open-docket list is on mass.gov, which blocks automated fetch, so it was swept through search; recent cases are mostly 69/115 kV rebuilds and BESS ties.
process_notes.CT: The Connecticut Siting Council issues certificates (Dockets) for new lines of 69 kV+ and declaratory rulings (Petitions) for modifications in existing ROW; the case lists are at portal.ct.gov/csc. Recent 345 kV petitions are structure/OPGW replacements, mostly without reconductoring.
process_notes.RI: The Energy Facility Siting Board (R.I.G.L. 42-98) licenses major energy facilities including lines of 69 kV+; dockets SB-YYYY-NN are on ripuc.ri.gov (blocks automated fetch). Only SB-2026-03 (332 line, listed) is 345 kV; SB-2025-01/03/04/05 and SB-2026-01 are 115 kV.
process_notes.NY: The PSC certifies lines of 100 kV+ over 10 miles (125 kV+ over 1 mile) under PSL Article VII (DPS active-case table); since the RAPID Act, new applications go to ORES under PSL Article VIII (rules effective Feb-Mar 2026, none filed in 2025). ORES also permits generators and their POI switchyards, and the NYISO queue and TO Local Transmission Plans cover the rest.
process_notes.PA: The Pennsylvania PUC sites HV lines (100 kV+) under 52 Pa. Code Chapter 57 Subchapter G: full siting applications (A-dockets, with prehearing conferences/public input hearings noticed in the Pennsylvania Bulletin) or Letters of Notification for short (<2 mi) taps and rebuilds; cases are searchable at puc.pa.gov document search and in the PA Bulletin 'Transmission Line' notices.
process_notes.NJ: New Jersey has no transmission-line certificate; utilities seek local land-use approvals or petition the BPU under N.J.S.A. 40:55D-19 for a 'reasonably necessary' finding that overrides local zoning (BPU dockets EO/EE). Offshore-wind SAA onshore upgrades (e.g., JCP&L NJCEC) are tracked through BPU SAA quarterly reports.
process_notes.MD: The Maryland PSC issues CPCNs for lines over 69 kV (Case No. 9xxx) with DNR Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) review; the PSC 'Energy Generation and Transmission Siting (CPCN) Cases' page and PPRP 'Projects Under Review' list all pending transmission cases.
process_notes.DE: Delaware has no state siting/certificate process for transmission lines; the Delaware PSC does not approve routes, so Delmarva Power and other developers need county/municipal land-use approvals and state environmental permits. Sources are Delmarva/PJM project lists and county records.
process_notes.DC: The DC PSC reviews Pepco transmission/substation projects through Formal Cases (e.g., FC 1144 Capital Grid) and DC zoning; there is no separate siting certificate list.
process_notes.VA: The State Corporation Commission issues CPCNs for lines over 138 kV under Code 56-46.1 and the Utility Facilities Act (cases PUR-YYYY-NNNNN); its Transmission Line Projects page lists recent cases by region, the Public Comments page lists open cases, and DocketSearch holds filings. Substations are mostly under local land-use review.
process_notes.WV: The Public Service Commission of West Virginia grants certificates of convenience and necessity (W. Va. Code 24-2-11 / 24-2-11a for 200 kV+ lines) in cases numbered YY-NNNN-E-CN; smaller rebuilds often proceed under General Order 265 notices or waivers (E-CN-PW). Cases are searchable on the PSC WebDocket.
process_notes.OH: The Ohio Power Siting Board (OPSB) certifies lines of 100 kV and up: full certificate applications (EL-BTX, with pre-application notification letters, public info meetings and local/adjudicatory hearings), and accelerated letters of notification (EL-BLN) and construction notices (EL-BNR) for shorter or in-ROW work. Case lists are on opsb.ohio.gov/cases and the PUCO DIS docket (dis.puc.state.oh.us), browsable by purpose code BTX/BLN/BNR/BTA.
process_notes.KY: The Kentucky PSC grants CPCNs for utility lines (KRS 278.020; lines of 138 kV+ and over a mile need one), and the State Board on Electric Generation and Transmission Siting (Siting Board, staffed by the PSC) issues construction certificates for merchant plants and nonregulated lines (KRS 278.700-.716). Both sets of cases are in the PSC case search (psc.ky.gov/Case/searchCases/<year>), with merchant cases under category 'Merchant Plant Applications'.
process_notes.MI: MPSC grants Act 30 certificates only for lines over 5 miles at 345 kV+ (cases U-xxxxx in MPSC e-dockets; METC filed U-22269 Oneida-Sabine Lake on 2026-11-04); other lines and substations are sited by ITC/METC/Consumers/DTE with local township approvals, and data-center service contracts go to the MPSC as special-contract cases (e.g. U-22058).
process_notes.IN: Indiana has no state siting certificate for transmission lines; the IURC rules on transmission-only utility status and eminent domain (e.g. WVTC Cause 46387), TDSIC cost-recovery plans that name line projects (Duke Cause 45647 TED sub-dockets) and large-load special contracts (NIPSCO Cause 46322). Cases are on the IURC online services portal (iurc.portal.in.gov); routes come from utility open houses.
process_notes.IL: Illinois Commerce Commission issues CPCNs for new lines under Sections 8-406 (standard) and 8-406.1 (expedited 150/225-day); cases are on the ICC e-Docket (icc.illinois.gov/docket), searchable by utility entity case lists. ComEd is in PJM; Ameren/ATXI and others are in MISO.
process_notes.WI: Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approves lines via CPCN (Wis. Stat. 196.491, 345 kV/large projects) or Certificate of Authority (196.49); dockets 137-CE (ATC), 4220-CE (NSPW), 1515-CE (Dairyland), 98xx-CE (merchant generators) are in PSC ERF/CMS, with major ones on the Highlighted Cases page.
process_notes.MN: Minnesota PUC issues certificates of need (CN) and route permits (TL) for lines over 100 kV (Minn. Stat. 216I since 2024; local units may permit some lines under 345 kV); dockets are on eDockets and the PUC Energy Infrastructure Permitting site (puc.eip.mn.gov/projects).
process_notes.IA: Iowa Utilities Commission grants electric transmission line franchises under Iowa Code ch. 478 (E-dockets in EFS at efs.iowa.gov) after a mandatory public informational meeting; hearings are held when eminent domain is sought or objections are filed.
process_notes.MO: AECI and its six G&T members are not Missouri PSC-regulated for line siting (no CCN cases); their 161/345 kV projects show up only in USDA RUS environmental reviews, SERTP/SPP study reports and co-op news. No public AECI project list was found.
process_notes.AR: Arkansas PSC issues a Certificate of Environmental Compatibility and Public Need (CECPN, Ark. Code 23-18-501, Utility Facility Environmental and Economic Protection Act) for lines over 100 kV and 1 mile; co-ops sometimes file CCNs. Dockets 'YY-NNN-U' at apps.apsc.arkansas.gov/olsv2.
process_notes.LA: Louisiana has no line-siting statute; the LPSC certifies transmission only through its Transmission Siting Order (2024; projects over set cost/length) and in generation/large-load certification dockets ('U-NNNNN'), many now under the 2025 'Lightning Initiative'. Docket portal lpscpubvalence.lpsc.louisiana.gov.
process_notes.MS: TVA lines in Mississippi are not MPSC-regulated; TVA sites them itself through its open-house / NEPA process (tva.com transmission projects and NEPA reviews). xAI's Southaven (MZX Tech) plant feeds Colossus 2 over private lines under DeSoto County easements; no state siting case.
process_notes.KS: The Kansas Corporation Commission issues siting permits under the Electric Transmission Line Siting Act (K.S.A. 66-1,177 et seq.) for lines of 230 kV and up and longer than 5 miles; dockets carry the -STG suffix (e.g., 26-EKCE-0148-STG) and hearings are announced in KCC news releases. Shorter/lower-voltage lines and substations need no state siting permit.
process_notes.NE: Nebraska has no route-siting proceeding for in-territory lines: the Power Review Board only approves lines built more than 1/2 mile outside the applicant's service area (its 2024-2026 approvals were all 69 kV or below), so NPPD/OPPD/LES lines are tracked through utility routing processes (open houses, public hearings) and SPP NTCs.
process_notes.ND: The ND Public Service Commission issues a Certificate of Corridor Compatibility and Route Permit (NDCC ch. 49-22) for lines over 115 kV, usually as a consolidated application under case numbers PU-YY-NNN; cases are on apps.psc.nd.gov and hearings in PSC news releases.
process_notes.SD: The SD Public Utilities Commission issues energy/transmission facility permits (SDCL 49-41B) for lines of 115 kV and up, under EL-YY-NNN dockets; utilities with SPP/MISO assignments also file informational notices of intent (ROFR) in the PUC's Informational dockets.
process_notes.MT: Montana DEQ issues Major Facility Siting Act certificates for lines over 69 kV, but exempts lines of 230 kV or less and 10 miles or less, upgrades of existing lines, substations, generator ties under 150 miles and lines with 75% ROW secured; the only active MFSA transmission case is North Plains Connector (certificate Sept 22, 2026). The Montana PSC does not site lines, so BPA NEPA reviews and NorthWestern plans are the main sources.
process_notes.AZ: The Arizona Power Plant and Transmission Line Siting Committee hears Certificate of Environmental Compatibility (CEC) applications for lines 115 kV+ (dockets L-xxxxx-YY-NNNN-00NNN, case numbers 185-272 since 2020) and the ACC votes to approve; the case calendar is at azcc.gov/arizona-power-plant/hearings-and-meetings and decisions appear in ACC open meeting highlights. Most 2023-2026 cases are developer gen-ties; nearly all were already in Line Watch.
process_notes.CA: CPUC approves investor-owned and CAISO-competitive lines via CPCN (200 kV+) or Permit to Construct (50-200 kV) applications (A.YY-MM-NNN) under GO 131-E with CEQA review by Energy Division (current-projects list plus quarterly GO 131-E utility reports); the CEC can permit generator ties through its Opt-In program; municipal utilities (LADWP, SMUD, IID, TID, etc.) approve their own lines as CEQA lead agencies, and BLM handles NEPA on federal land. Ironwood (North Gila-Imperial Valley #2 500 kV, A.25-09-008, filed Sept 2025), Recon/North of SONGS substation, Golden Pacific Powerlink (CPCN due Q4 2026) and Orange Regional (NoSS) are all due Dec 2031 or later, so they were left out.
process_notes.NM: The NM PRC grants CCNs (NMSA 62-9-1), location approval for 230 kV+ lines, and right-of-way width determinations over 100 ft (62-9-3.2), in dockets like 26-0000137 searchable on PRCe360 (e360.prc.nm.gov); the NM Renewable Energy Transmission Authority (RETA) co-develops merchant lines (SunZia, Crossroads-Hobbs-Roadrunner, RioSol, Mora Line, Hidden Mountain Extension, North Path).
process_notes.NV: The PUCN issues Utility Environmental Protection Act (UEPA) permits to construct lines over 200 kV (and gen-ties) on non-federal land, and developers must file a UEPA notice when they apply to BLM/another federal agency for lines on federal land; dockets are YY-MMNNN at pucweb1.state.nv.us. NV Energy lines are first approved in IRP amendments (e.g. 24-05041, 26-05007) and BLM grants ROW via ePlanning NEPA reviews.
process_notes.CO: Colorado PUC grants CPCNs for transmission (proceedings 2XA-XXXXE; Rule 3206 filings decide whether a CPCN is needed, and the Rule 3627 10-year plan in 26M-0051E lists every project), while counties and cities approve routes through 1041 / location-and-extent permits; case list at the PUC E-Filings system (dora.state.co.us/pls/efi).
process_notes.UT: Utah has no state line-siting certificate for most utility lines; Rocky Mountain Power gets local conditional-use permits (e.g., Utah County CU2025-05) after the Utah Code 54-18 notice process, with the Utah PSC only resolving siting disputes and IRP/acknowledgment; BLM handles federal-land rights of way.
process_notes.WY: Wyoming PSC issues CPCNs for utility lines and substations (dockets 2000x-xxx-EN-yy, notices at psc.wyo.gov/home/public-notices), and the DEQ Industrial Siting Council permits facilities above the cost threshold (DEQ/ISC dockets), which covers most large generator gen-ties.
process_notes.ID: Idaho PUC issues CPCNs (cases IPC-E-/PAC-E-/AVU-E-yy-nn) for new utility transmission; routes are approved through county conditional/special-use permits and BLM/USFS NEPA on federal land.
process_notes.OR: Oregon EFSC issues site certificates for transmission lines of 230 kV+ and more than 10 miles (ODOE facility pages and monthly EFSC Project Updates), Oregon PUC issues CPCNs when condemnation is needed (AR 626 rules), and shorter lines go through county conditional-use permits.
process_notes.WA: Washington EFSEC certifies large energy facilities and, since 2023, may site electrical transmission on an opt-in basis (efsec.wa.gov facility list); otherwise lines are permitted by counties/cities, with BPA lines reviewed under NEPA; the UTC does not site lines.
process_notes.NC: NCUC issues certificates of environmental compatibility and public convenience and necessity (G.S. 62-100 et seq., Rule R8-62) for lines of 161 kV and up, in dockets E-2 Sub (DEP), E-7 Sub (DEC), EC- (co-ops) and EMP- (merchant gen-ties); the hearings page https://www.ncuc.gov/hearings/hearings.html lists open cases, but the NCUC document server (starw1.ncuc.gov) returned 403 to direct fetches, so individual orders could not be read.
process_notes.SC: PSC of South Carolina certifies lines of 125 kV and up under the Utility Facility Siting and Environmental Protection Act (S.C. Code 58-33), with 'like facility' determinations for rebuilds; cases are in DMS (https://dms.psc.sc.gov), whose docket search is reCAPTCHA-protected, so cases were found through docket and order pages surfaced by search.
process_notes.FL: Lines of 230 kV+ that cross a county line and run 15+ miles go through a PSC need determination (s. 403.537) and then DEP Siting Coordination Office / Siting Board certification under the Transmission Line Siting Act (TA numbers); single-county lines need neither, so utility project pages and Ten Year Site Plans cover the rest.
process_notes.GA: No state line-siting approval: the GA PSC only reviews transmission in Georgia Power's IRP (Docket 56002); GTC, Georgia Power and MEAG publish project pages and legal notices of open houses before condemnation (O.C.G.A. 22-3-160.1), and RUS environmental assessments cover GTC lines.
process_notes.AL: No state line-siting process at the Alabama PSC; sources are Alabama Power/PowerSouth project information, DOE Loan Programs Office NEPA records for Alabama Power's loan-funded projects, SERTP, and TVA project pages for north Alabama.
process_notes.TN: TVA approves its own lines (NEPA EAs/CEs and the TVA transmission project pages, https://tva.com/energy/transmission/transmission-system-projects); the TPUC grants CCNs only to non-TVA public utilities (e.g., Kingsport Power/AEP, in PJM) and no qualifying TPUC line case was found.
process_notes.AK: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska regulates Railbelt utilities and the new Railbelt Transmission Organization (Docket U-25-028), but there is no separate line-siting certificate; projects come through AEA (Bradley Lake PMC, Intertie, CIPLink, Beluga-Healy) and utility (Chugach, HEA, MEA, GVEA) programs.
process_notes.HI: The Hawaii PUC must approve new overhead lines of 46 kV and up (HRS 269-27.5/27.6, with specific findings for 138 kV+); recent cases are 46 kV (e.g., Dkt 2025-0436), and no new 138 kV Oahu line in an application or construction stage was found; 69 kV lines on Maui and Hawaii Island do not count.
